after_plain: Events the tool loses on a full disk are now kept in a lasting record that a restart shows.
A torn last line left by a full disk is now closed by the next write, so no event vanishes.
A closed error stream no longer crashes the server, the command tool or a download; the lost line is counted.
The saved copy of an unreadable vendor reply is now named in the log and kept safely on disk.
A corrupt data page is now refused with a reason instead of crashing the reader.
A time index is now tied to the exact bar file it belongs to, so a swapped index is refused.
Not-a-number and infinite values in the log now read back as numbers.
A log line that repeats a field is now refused by name, and the writer never repeats one.
The server opens a browser only when asked; otherwise it just prints the address.
An oversized catalogue is now refused for its size, which is the true reason.
Asking for bars past the end of a month now reads one record, not the whole month.
A lasting top-results refusal now costs one record read per request, not a full walk.
The trade readers are kept on purpose and their cost is now timed with one shared tool.
The verify page now checks one page of at most 1,024 months per request.
The verify page now checks one page of at most 1,024 months per request.
A request's query text is now split once, not once for every field.
The live sweep status page is now tested and timed at its largest allowed sizes.
Refreshing masters when nothing changed no longer rebuilds the whole universe.
Highs and lows over a time window now come from kept monthly summaries; other sorts stop at a stated ceiling.
The audit journal's cost is now measured as it grows; whether to rotate old files is your call.
An evidence page now proves it is current through the same read that serves it.
A qualification page now shows at most 16,384 folds.
An unreadable server lock note is now named as unreadable, not called missing.
The first record of a journal or new results file now makes its folder entry safe on disk.
Every sweep launch route now logs when it refuses an unstamped build.
A blocked recovery now logs its stage and reason.
Every contract download that fails is now logged with its reason.
A pull run refused before it starts is now logged with its reason.
A run's log now shows only the events that belong to that run.
The multi-feed pull now logs each step and how it ended.
The autopilot now logs when it halts, stalls or stops.
Every store check is now logged, and the database page can run one.
Every network retry is now logged once with its reason.
A crash mid-save no longer blocks nine ledgers; the torn end is cut and logged.
A sweep refused by its required audit is now logged, and the finish line carries the real exit code.
A crash now leaves one event in the log before the program stops.
Very large ranked result files can now still be read page by page.
The build file no longer claims the command tool has no loops.
Each out-of-sample check no longer re-derives its group's identity.
The record now says plainly that a held writer does not re-read old rows, and a test proves it.
The unused best-results keeper was removed, so its cost no longer exists.
Scripts hidden in data links or embedded frames are now refused by the checks.
A workflow step can no longer hand a ready-made action a program to run.
The run settings file is now read by a check and may hold only the two allowed settings.

Exchange test listings are now caught whatever their spacing or letter case.
Lower-case exchange test listings are now caught too.
Whole numbers with any number of zero decimals read again; a real fraction is refused by name.
The merged log page no longer claims it reached the oldest event when it cut results.
An unreadable master file is now shown as unreadable, not missing.
A session cache entry is now saved to disk before it is called safe.
A failed index append now says how many entries actually landed.
Live sweep progress now reads only its own run, so old log damage no longer blocks it.
Each month refused during a sweep-all run now leaves a log line with its reason.
A refused stored-month sweep now logs its reason.
The command-finished log line now says why a command was refused.
The ingest page now reads a stop that was taken but not saved, and shows its warning.
The audit page now names an older page it could not read instead of counting it.
One refused index row no longer drops the rest of the batch.
The saved-evidence panel now shows the server's reason for a refusal.
Six web pages now show the server's refusal reason and keep an unknown as unknown, not zero.
A save-to-disk step for the log now exists, but the server and command tool do not call it at exit yet.
